questions.question: I've uploaded my market research and concept. Before I write the BRD: which existing systems does the Wire Tracking Center depend on, and who owns each today?

fact_pass_matrix.desc: gpi connector current owner is GTSI (not PNE/Raj Malhotra)

runs_detail.answer:
Scope: "the Wire Tracking Center" = the CBO Wire Center module (SYS-CBO), per current-state architecture doc CBO-ARCH-WC-4.1 (v4.1, approved, last reviewed 2026-08-20, owner Lucas Ferreira). System owners: business owner Marcus Chen; technical co-owners Tom Becker & Lucas Ferreira (CBO Wire Center squad), under Anjali Deshpande (Dir., Digital Treasury Channels Engineering).

DEPENDENCIES IT ACTUALLY HAS TODAY (what cbo-wire-bff calls live):
1. PRISM Payments Hub (PPH) — v1 Wire Status API (EP-PPH-01/02/03) — owner: Payments Hub Engineering. Submission, activity list, status lookup. Note: PPH v1 is deprecated, sunset 2027-03-31 (no extensions); the v2 migration (CBO-4471) is unscheduled.
2. Commercial Entitlements Service (CES, EP-CES-01) — owner: CBO Platform & Entitlements (EM Nadia Haddad, Tech Lead Arjun Mehta). Authorization/account filtering.
3. CBO Auth Step-Up API (EP-AUTH-01) — owning platform is named only as "CBO Auth" in the wiki; no specific team/person is documented beyond that. Gates wire release.
4. Enterprise Notification Service (ENS, EP-ENS-01) — owner: Enterprise Notification Platform (Director Sanjay Iyer). Produces TRS.WIRE.* notifications.

TRANSITIVE (systems PPH itself depends on, not called by Wire Center directly): Core Deposit Platform (owner: Deposits Data Ownership), Fedwire Funds Connector (owner: Payment Networks Engineering), Hold Management Service/HMS (owner: Financial Crimes Technology), Swift gpi Connector (owner: Global Transaction Services Integration/GTSI).

GAPS — systems your FC-02/03/04 assumptions rely on that Wire Center does NOT integrate with today (flag these for the BRD):
- gpi/live route (FC-02): Swift gpi status is currently visible only to Payment Operations via the Investigations Workbench (per spike CBO-4480); there is no path to Wire Center clients today. The gpi feed itself is owned by GTSI (Swift gpi Connector), separate from Payment Networks Engineering, which ran the spike.
- Held-wire exact reason (FC-03): PPH v1's holdReasonDesc exists but is not surfaced to CBO; the true source of review reasons is the Hold Management Service (owner: Financial Crimes Technology), and ADR-PAY-021 ("Hold Reason Confidentiality") constrains what can be shown to clients.
- Insights (FC-04): your assumption that insights can be computed in the CBO wire BFF conflicts with ADR-PAY-026, which requires client-facing analytics to be served via the TDIP Insights API (owner: Treasury Data & Insights Platform), not computed locally in a channel BFF. TDIP's only GA endpoint today is cash-forecast; no wire-history/corridor-insights endpoint exists yet.
- CBO Status Projection Service (SPS, owner: CBO Platform & Entitlements) is ACH-only today; not wired for wires despite being the natural basis for a FC-01-style timeline.

Net: Wire Center's actual current dependency set is PPH v1, CES, CBO Auth, and ENS, each with a different owning team than the systems FC-02/03/04 assume access to (gpi/GTSI, HMS/FCT, TDIP). These are the teams to engage before finalizing BRD scope and estimates.</answer>
<parameter name="confidence">high
